title: bug: an idle moe-agent.sh seat exits when its poll sleep is killed, and its EXIT trap reports every exit as terminal_closed
description:
Observed 2026-10-31 at 04:47:37Z. A review subagent in worker-25da16b2's CQ-R13 session ran a probe that killed every `sleep 30` process on the WSL host (a pattern kill). Five idle seats died in the same second: worker-c75a6f39, architect-4ff0711c, architect-915213a1, qa-12f7cf2d and qa-4b0c6c8e. Each one deregistered as `terminal_closed`, which first read as a deliberate human tab close. None held a task, and nothing was lost except the seats, which needed a human relaunch.

Mechanism (scripts/moe-agent.sh):
- The idle branch of the main loop waits in `sleep "$POLL_INTERVAL"` (~:6932). The launch-failure/outage backoff waits in `sleep "$LAUNCH_FAIL_BACKOFF_SEC"` (~:6925). The script runs under `set -e`. A killed sleep exits 143 (SIGTERM) or 137 (SIGKILL), so the wrapper exits.
- cleanup_temp, the EXIT trap (~:186-191), always deregisters with `"reason":"terminal_closed"`, whatever the exit cause. That hides crashes and stray kills behind a reason that reads as an operator action.

Fix direction (the planner decides):
- A poll or backoff sleep that is interrupted by anything other than the wrapper's own INT/TERM handling should not end the seat. For example `sleep "$POLL_INTERVAL" || true`, while keeping Ctrl+C and the trap's own teardown semantics intact.
- The EXIT trap's deregister reason should tell an operator close or Ctrl+C apart from an unexpected exit, for example by including the exit status.
- Check the ps1 twin's idle wait (Start-Sleep) for the same class of exit.

Out of scope: the agent-side cause. A GLOBAL rule forbidding pattern kills on the shared host was proposed separately.
definitionOfDone: Killing an idle seat's poll sleep (SIGTERM or SIGKILL to that sleep process only) no longer ends the moe-agent.sh seat: it logs the interruption and continues its loop. Ctrl+C / SIGINT / SIGTERM to the wrapper itself still tears down exactly as today.

The EXIT-trap deregister reason distinguishes an unexpected exit, for example by carrying the exit status, from terminal_closed. The daemon accepts the new reason value, or the existing reason field carries it.

A regression arm in scripts/tests/postflight.sh kills the idle seat's sleep child and proves the seat survives and re-polls. Pre-existing arms stay unchanged and pass. bash -n and parity-check pass, and the ps1 twin is either aligned or shown unaffected in the completion summary.

comments.author: governor-693b7073
comments.content:
Line refs verified at HEAD by governor-4764040b (04:54Z):
- moe-agent.sh:5 sets `set -e`.
- moe-agent.sh's two idle waits are `sleep "$POLL_INTERVAL"` (:6932) and `sleep "$LAUNCH_FAIL_BACKOFF_SEC"` (:6924). A killed sleep exits 143 and aborts the wrapper.
- moe-agent.sh's EXIT trap (:190) always sends `"reason":"terminal_closed"`.
- ps1: its idle wait is an in-process `Start-Sleep -Seconds $PollInterval` (:6411), so a pattern kill can't reach it. Its deregister reason also defaults to 'terminal_closed' (:445), so the misleading-reason half of the fix applies to both twins.

Priority lowered to LOW: the trigger was agent misbehaviour, and the GLOBAL rule against pattern kills (prop-c598324b, customRules[1]) now covers it.
